purpose: ASVS 5.0 V11.1.2 asks the cryptographic inventory to record where each key may and may not be used and what data it may and may not protect. The generated inventory answers what exists and where it appears; that is discoverable by scanning. This answers what each key is for, which is not - so it is written here and held to the generated inventory by scripts/security/verify-key-usage.mjs. A key that spreads to a new file fails the build until the decision is revisited.

keys.name: ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET
mayProtect: Nothing that this repository mints. The commercial-surface actor reader in the web tier verifies tokens under it, and no code here issues one
mustNotProtect: Platform access tokens, which are signed under JWT_SECRET. The API's env validation requires this name while no API code signs with it - recorded rather than silently tidied away

keys.name: AI_ASSISTANT_API_KEY
mayProtect: Nothing. It authenticates to the model provider
mustNotProtect: Any application data. It is a third-party service credential

keys.name: AI_ASSISTANT_MAX_TOKENS
mayProtect: Nothing. It is a request budget
mustNotProtect: Any data. It is configuration that matches the key-material pattern by name and is kept and labelled rather than silently dropped

keys.name: AUTH_MAIL_OUTBOX_CURRENT_KEY_VERSION
mayProtect: Nothing. It selects which keyring version is current
mustNotProtect: Any data. It is configuration

keys.name: AUTH_MAIL_OUTBOX_CURRENT_KEY_VERSION_FILE
mayProtect: Nothing. It names the file holding the current version pointer
mustNotProtect: Any data. It is configuration

keys.name: AUTH_MAIL_OUTBOX_KEY
mayProtect: Auth-mail outbox payloads at rest, under a versioned keyring where each version derives its own key
mustNotProtect: Any credential or session material. This contour encrypts queued mail, not anything that admits a request

keys.name: AUTH_MAIL_OUTBOX_KEYRING_DIR
mayProtect: Nothing. It names where the keyring lives
mustNotProtect: Any data. It is configuration, not key material, and is inventoried because where a key lives is part of an inventory

keys.name: BANK_HMAC_SECRET
mayProtect: Bank callback authenticity, as the legacy single-key entry in a registry that accepts several keys at once with validity windows
mustNotProtect: Any session, credential or application data at rest. It authenticates an inbound counterparty message and nothing else

keys.name: CRM_WEBHOOK_TOKEN
mayProtect: Lead delivery to CRM, as the legacy name behind PLATFORM_V7_CRM_WEBHOOK_TOKEN
mustNotProtect: Anything in the platform contour

keys.name: DEAL_REGISTRY_CURSOR_SECRET
mayProtect: Deal-registry pagination cursors, binding a cursor to the filter set it was issued for, signed under a key derived from this material by HKDF rather than under the material itself
mustNotProtect: Any session or credential. Its fallback to JWT_SECRET when unset was a boundary violation raised as #4790; the fallback remains, but domain separation means the signing key differs from the session-signing secret whichever material is in use

keys.name: EDO_WEBHOOK_SECRET
mayProtect: EDO webhook authenticity, as an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the raw request body
mustNotProtect: Any session or credential material, and any other integration's webhooks - each integration authenticates under its own secret

keys.name: GEKTA_ANONYMOUS_SESSION_SECRET
mayProtect: Anonymous Gekta browsing sessions, which carry no identity and no entitlement
mustNotProtect: Any authenticated session. An anonymous session must never be upgradable into one by re-signing

keys.name: GEKTA_PHONE_ENCRYPTION_KEY
mayProtect: Stored phone numbers, encrypted at rest with a 32-byte key
mustNotProtect: Lookup indexes. Searching by phone uses a separate pepper, so the encryption key never has to be present to answer a lookup

keys.name: GEKTA_PHONE_LOOKUP_PEPPER
mayProtect: The blind index that makes a stored phone number searchable without decrypting it
mustNotProtect: The phone numbers themselves. It produces a lookup value, never plaintext, and cannot reverse one

keys.name: JWT_SECRET
mayProtect: Platform and Gekta access tokens, signed and verified as HS256 with a stated algorithm allowlist
Cabinet session cookies in the web tier, which select which role's pages render and grant no API access
The MFA secret encryption key, derived from this material inside auth-crypto
mustNotProtect: Opaque one-time credentials. Password reset, MFA recovery, invitation, email verification, membership selection, refresh, MFA challenge, registration status, backup code and staff access digests derive a separate key by HKDF under a purpose label, and the API refuses to start in production without a dedicated key for it

Anything outside the authentication contour. Its reuse as the deal-registry cursor fallback was a boundary violation, raised as #4790 and closed: the cursor now derives its own key by HKDF under pc-deal-registry-cursor:v1, so this material signs no cursor even when it is the material the cursor key is derived from

keys.name: MARKETING_TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
mayProtect: Telegram marketing webhook authenticity
mustNotProtect: Anything in the platform contour. The marketing surface holds no authority over deals, money or identity

keys.name: MFA_LOGIN_TICKET_SECRET
mayProtect: Short-lived MFA login tickets in the web tier, minimum 32 characters enforced at read time
mustNotProtect: Any session that survives the MFA step. A ticket carries a pending challenge, not an authenticated identity

keys.name: ORGANIZATION_INVITATION_DELIVERY_KEY
mayProtect: The delivery boundary for organization invitations and MFA-recovery mail: proof that the caller is the mail delivery path
mustNotProtect: The invitation credential itself, which is minted and digested by the opaque token authority under its own key

keys.name: PASSWORD_RESET_DELIVERY_KEY
mayProtect: The delivery boundary for password-reset mail
mustNotProtect: The reset credential itself, and any other delivery contour - registration and invitation each hold their own key

keys.name: PC_ACCEPTANCE_JWT_SECRET
mayProtect: Tokens inside the acceptance browser matrix only
mustNotProtect: Anything production reaches. It exists so acceptance never borrows a real signing secret

keys.name: PC_ACCEPTANCE_TLS_KEY
mayProtect: The TLS key of the local HTTPS server the acceptance matrix runs against
mustNotProtect: Any production endpoint. It is generated for the run and never leaves it

keys.name: PC_CABINET_SESSION_SECRET
mayProtect: Cabinet session cookies, but only as a fallback when JWT_SECRET is unset
mustNotProtect: Anything on its own. It is a fallback name for the same material rather than a separate key, so it inherits every boundary JWT_SECRET has

keys.name: PLATFORM_V7_CRM_WEBHOOK_TOKEN
mayProtect: Lead delivery to CRM, preferred over the legacy name
mustNotProtect: Anything in the platform contour

keys.name: REGISTRATION_DELIVERY_KEY
mayProtect: The delivery boundary for registration and registration-decision mail
mustNotProtect: The registration credential itself, and any other delivery contour

keys.name: RESEND_API_KEY
mayProtect: Nothing. It authenticates to the Resend mail provider
mustNotProtect: Any application data. It is a third-party service credential

keys.name: TAI_PLATFORM_TOOL_HMAC_SECRET_B64
mayProtect: Tool-call assertions between the platform and the Gekta tool runtime
mustNotProtect: User sessions and any credential a person presents. It binds a machine-to-machine assertion

keys.name: VAULT_TOKEN
mayProtect: Nothing directly. It authenticates this application to HashiCorp Vault's transit engine
mustNotProtect: Any application data. It is a credential to an external service, and the material Vault holds never becomes this token
